notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Shorter than normal white plates with the blue EU strip on the left.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Long black-and-white bollards with a rectangular white reflector on the front, two dots on the back and a usually diagonal black strip; round or thin and curved.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Orange snow poles with one thin white band near the top; neighbours to the west have a much wider band lower down.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Outer road lines are always solid white, unlike the dashed ones in the western neighbours.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Middle lines include white dashes, solid yellow with white dashes and double yellow; yellow is being phased out.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Road signs have a yellow background.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Signs with a red border have a thin yellow stroke at the edge, seen in no other Nordic country.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian signs have 5 stripes.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are solid blue with white text and a white border incorporating guiding arrows.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are black with yellow arrows.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Bus stop signs are blue and white or yellow and black, rarely with stop names.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Traffic signposts often have blue and white striped markings.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Looks unlike most European languages: long words, double vowels, and ä and ö; streets end in tie or katu.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Mostly wooden poles with simple tops, often carrying a street light fixed at the top with a double bolt.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dense boreal forest of pine and white-trunked birch, and lakes everywhere.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Much generation 3 was shot in autumn, a fall look that is rare in the other Nordics.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Modern, utilitarian buildings, concrete apartment blocks downtown, detached wooden-clad houses in suburbs, and some dark red wooden buildings in the countryside.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: K-Market and S-Market supermarket logos appear, chains found only here.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Includes the low-quality Ari camera with a wide round blur and brownish colours, plus smallcam coverage.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Regional roads have 3 or 4 digits whose first digit rises from 1 in the south to 9 in the north.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Snow poles with two long reflectors on bigger roads in Lapland, only in 2023 coverage or later.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Most farmland is concentrated near the west and south coasts.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Wind turbines are most common along the west coast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Small stunted trees with thin spindly trunks are common in the far north.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Regular generation 3 snow coverage exists only in far northwestern Lapland.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Along some southern and western coasts, signs are bilingual with the neighbour's language; do not guess inland if you see it.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Bilingual signs with Sámi place names appear in the far north, using the letter c.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A slightly tilted long antenna occurs in the southwest; generation 3 with no antenna is found in south-central areas.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The island group in the southwest is monolingual in the neighbour's language, has no generation 4, red-tinted pavement and dashed outer lines.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Island plates are short, fully white with blue text and no EU strip.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Road 970 in the far north follows a river valley with stunted birches on the Norwegian border.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The far northwest near the Scandinavian Mountains has hilly terrain with low vegetation.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The capital has unique green-and-yellow trams; Tampere's are red.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Buses vary by city: blue-and-white split in the capital, NYSSE in Tampere, yellow in Turku, green in Jyväskylä, pink-fronted in Oulu.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Red metal plates with 7 protrusions in a rounded hexagon appear on houses and posts in Tampere.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Lahti uses black-bordered all-caps street signs; Kerava and Järvenpää show coats of arms in the corner; Seinäjoki has unique blue ones.
